Scanning a signature with your phone

Get a clean signature image for an exam form using only a phone, with a white background and no scanner needed.

Sign it properly first

Use plain white unlined paper. Ruled or graph paper leaves lines in the image that no amount of processing removes cleanly. A black or dark blue pen with a reasonably thick nib works best. Gel and ballpoint are both fine. Pencil and light coloured ink disappear once the image is compressed.

Sign larger than you normally would, filling perhaps a third of an A4 sheet. The image gets scaled down to something like 140 by 60 pixels, and a small signature turns to mush at that size while a large one stays legible.

Use your ordinary signature. Whatever you upload has to match what you write on the OMR sheet and attendance register on exam day, and a mismatch can cost you your candidature. This is not the moment to invent a neater version of yourself.

Photographing it

Put the paper on a flat surface in daylight, near a window but not in direct sun, which creates harsh shadows and blown out highlights. Turn the flash off. Flash flattens the ink and creates a bright hotspot in the middle of the page.

Hold the phone directly above the paper, parallel to it. Shooting at an angle makes the signature look skewed and no crop fixes the distortion. Watch your own shadow. Standing between the window and the paper puts you in the picture whether you like it or not.

Tap the screen on the signature before you shoot, which locks focus and exposure onto the ink rather than the bright paper.

Getting the paper to read as white

This is where most phone captures fall down. Your eye sees white paper. The camera records light grey, because it exposes for the overall scene and paper reflects less light than you assume. Some portals run a contrast check and bounce the result.

The fix is to push everything above a brightness threshold to pure white while leaving the dark ink untouched. Our resizer has a checkbox for exactly this, and it is switched on by default on signature presets. If you prefer to do it elsewhere, most photo editors achieve the same thing with a strong levels or curves adjustment.

Cropping and sizing

Crop reasonably tight around the signature, leaving a small margin. Do not crop so close that the ink touches the edge, because some portals treat that as a truncated image.

Then set the exact pixel dimensions your form asks for. Signatures are usually wide and short, something like 140 by 60, which is a very different shape from anything your phone camera produces. Choose the option that keeps the whole signature and pads with white rather than the one that crops to fill, or you will lose the ends of your own name.

A note on scanner apps

Document scanner apps often apply aggressive sharpening and contrast that can break thin pen strokes into dotted lines. If you use one, check the result at full zoom before you commit. A plain camera photo processed properly is usually cleaner than an over-enhanced scan.
